coverage.notes: SEL: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce page lists 'Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards' (full document PDF dated June 2019, five CASEL-based competencies, topics A1-E4, benchmarks by grade band). Read the full PDF. POG: no statewide Portrait/Profile of a Graduate found on education.ohio.gov. The 2019-2024 strategic plan 'Each Child, Our Future' (read, p.29) has an appendix 'Framework for Attributes of a High School Graduate' but says local schools lead in identifying their graduates' attributes and that the list is a model to help schools build their own. Treated as district-led, so no portrait_of_graduate framework was recorded. Reviewer: confirm with ODEW that no newer statewide profile replaced it after the plan's 2024 end date.

frameworks.name: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards
frameworks.issuingBody: Ohio Department of Education (now Ohio Department of Education and Workforce)
frameworks.notes: Read from the full standards PDF linked on the ODEW SEL page (https://education.ohio.gov/getattachment/Topics/Learning-in-Ohio/Social-and-Emotional-Learning/K-12-SEL-Standards-Full.pdf.aspx?lang=en-US), title page 'June 2019'. Organized competency (A-E, the five CASEL competencies) > topic (18 topics, A1-E4) > grade-band standards (K-2, 3-5, middle grades, high school). Items here are the 18 topics, not the per-band standards; every topic applies across K-12. Conflict: the ODEW web page says bands are 'kindergarten-grade 3, grades 3-5', while the PDF says K-2 / 3-5; the PDF was followed. Adoption year left blank: the PDF gives only the June 2019 date, and State Board approval is stated only by a third-party news summary, so confirm the adoption date with ODEW. Titles and summaries are short paraphrases of the topic statements.

items.title: Awareness of personal emotions
items.summary: Identify, name and understand one's own emotions, how they affect others and when and where to process them safely.

items.title: Awareness of personal interests, qualities, strengths and challenges
items.summary: Recognize one's own interests, strengths and areas for growth.

items.title: Awareness of and willingness to seek help for self or others
items.summary: Know when help is needed and be willing to ask for it or offer it.

items.title: Personal responsibility, confidence and advocacy
items.summary: Take responsibility for one's actions, build confidence and speak up for oneself.

items.title: Regulate emotions and behaviors with thinking strategies
items.summary: Use strategies, suited to how the brain develops, to manage emotions and behavior.

items.title: Set, monitor, adapt and evaluate goals
items.summary: Set goals, track progress, adjust and reflect to succeed in school and life.

items.title: Persevere through challenges and setbacks
items.summary: Keep going through difficulty and recover from setbacks in school and life.

items.title: Recognize and empathize with others' feelings and perspectives
items.summary: Notice, name and respond with empathy to what others feel and think.

items.title: Consideration for and contribution to school, community and world
items.summary: Show care for others and contribute to the well-being of school, community and the wider world.

items.title: Awareness and respect for human dignity and differences
items.summary: Respect the similarities and differences among people, groups and cultures.

items.title: Read social cues and respond constructively
items.summary: Notice social cues and respond in helpful ways.

items.title: Positive verbal and non-verbal communication and social skills
items.summary: Communicate and interact effectively with others, one-on-one and in groups.

items.title: Develop and maintain positive relationships
items.summary: Build and keep healthy relationships with peers and adults.

items.title: Prevent, manage and resolve interpersonal conflict
items.summary: Handle and resolve conflicts with others in constructive ways.

items.title: Effective decision-making and critical thinking
items.summary: Develop, apply and model sound decision-making and critical thinking.

items.title: Identify potential outcomes to make constructive decisions
items.summary: Weigh likely consequences of choices before deciding.

items.title: Consider the ethical and civic impact of decisions
items.summary: Think about the ethical and civic effects of one's choices on self, others and community.

items.title: Approach new situations with an open mind and curiosity
items.summary: Explore unfamiliar situations with openness and curiosity, accepting that outcomes can be uncertain or uncomfortable.

alignments.framework: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Stay in Control of Your Spirit" (series: Conflict & Self-Government; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Learners will identify signs that emotions are beginning to take control, practice a simple pause-and-reset process, and choose one respectful action that keeps their response aligned with their values." The lesson has students recognise when emotions start driving behaviour and choose a response, which is the same skill.

target.title: Stay in Control of Your Spirit - Lesson Plan 10 - 23 - #155 - MS

alignments.framework: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards
alignments.rationale: Tune Your Brain game "Feelings Detective" (tagged self-awareness). FNE's catalog description: "Notice real cues in a scene, then pick every feeling that plausibly fits." Covers naming what someone feels from real cues; it does not by itself connect those feelings to the player's own actions.

alignments.framework: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards
alignments.rationale: Morning Boost program theme "Emotional Intelligence" (programs.html). FNE's published description: "Understanding and naming emotions, managing reactions, building empathy, and developing the self-awareness that underlies every other social-emotional skill." The theme names understanding emotions and self-awareness. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it.

alignments.framework: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards
alignments.rationale: FNE lesson "Ask for Help the Right Way" (series: Communication That Helps; the objective is the same in every grade version). FNE's stated objective: "Students will understand that needing help does not mean they are weak. It means they are honest enough to recognize when they need support. Students will learn to ask clearly, speak respectfully, listen carefully, and keep trying instead of shutting down or ..." Teaches asking clearly and respectfully and keeping going rather than shutting down, which includes seeking help.

target.title: Ask for Help the Right Way - Lesson Plan: 6 - 9 - #57_MS

alignments.framework: Ohio's K-12 Social and Emotional Learning Standards

FNE's published description: "Practical skills for managing time, setting goals, handling failure, asking for help, and preparing for adult responsibilities." The theme names asking for help. Program-level: shows the theme is part of the offering, not which lesson teaches it. Limit: Seeking help only; the standard also covers helping others.
